title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
title_zh: MedSkill-E²：评估与演化医疗智能体的技能
abstract_en: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills to access domain knowledge and complete real-world tasks. We observe that even when a skill specifies the rules and procedures needed for a task, agents may fail to apply them effectively during autonomous execution, a phenomenon we call skill Enable But Underuse (EBU). This issue is particularly consequential in medical tasks, where overlooking a single critical constraint can yield a plausible but incorrect result. To evaluate and address EBU, we introduce MedSkill-E$^{2}$, a framework for evaluating and evolving skills for medical agents. We construct EBU-Bench, a challenging benchmark covering 12 medically relevant task groups and associated skills, to evaluate agents' ability to use available skills autonomously. We quantify the EBU gap as the difference in skill-use accuracy between autonomous use and explicitly guided reading and application of the same skill. On EBU-Bench, all evaluated model-harness combinations exhibit EBU, with a mean gap of 43.94 percentage points (pp). For the same model, skill-use accuracy under autonomous use differs by up to 38.96 pp across harnesses. Motivated by these observations, we propose EBU-Evolve, which uses execution feedback from autonomous and explicitly guided skill use to distill effective guidance into reusable skill instructions. Relative to their pre-evolution versions, the revised skills improve skill-use accuracy during autonomous execution by 33.33 to 55.17 pp and continue to yield improvements when transferred across multiple models and harnesses. Our results show that autonomous skill-use accuracy varies across harnesses with the model and skill held fixed, and model rankings can change. EBU can persist even after a skill is opened. EBU-Evolve improves autonomous skill-use accuracy on unseen tasks within the same skill, with gains transferring across models and harnesses.
abstract_zh: 大语言模型智能体即使拥有写明任务规则与操作流程的技能，也可能在自主执行时未能有效应用其中的指令。论文将这一现象称为技能可用却未充分利用（skill Enable But Underuse，EBU）。在医疗任务中，遗漏一条关键约束就可能产生看似合理却错误的结果。为衡量并缓解 EBU，作者提出 MedSkill-E²，并构建覆盖 12 类医疗相关任务及配套技能的 EBU-Bench，将同一技能在自主使用与显式引导阅读和应用两种条件下的使用准确率之差定义为 EBU 差距。所有受测模型与智能体运行框架（harness）的组合均出现 EBU，平均差距为 43.94 个百分点；固定模型和技能时，不同运行框架下的自主技能使用准确率最多相差 38.96 个百分点。作者进一步提出 EBU-Evolve，从两种执行条件的反馈中提炼有效引导，将其写入可复用的技能指令。修订后的技能使自主使用准确率比修订前提高 33.33 至 55.17 个百分点，并在同一技能的未见任务上取得提升，收益也可迁移至其他模型和运行框架。
key_points_zh: EBU-Bench 覆盖 12 类医疗相关任务，通过对比同一技能在自主使用和显式引导下的使用准确率，量化技能未充分利用的程度。
所有受测组合的 EBU 差距平均为 43.94 个百分点；即使智能体已经打开技能，也可能未能正确应用其中的指令。
固定模型和技能后，更换运行框架可使自主技能使用准确率相差最多 38.96 个百分点，模型排名也可能随框架改变。
EBU-Evolve 将执行反馈转化为可复用的技能指令，使自主技能使用准确率提升 33.33 至 55.17 个百分点；改进可推广到同一技能的未见任务，并迁移到其他模型和运行框架。

agent-harness-evolution.reason: 核心贡献是利用自主执行与显式引导执行的反馈改写可复用技能，而非仅做静态评测。演化前后的量化对比显示，自主技能使用准确率提高了 33.33–55.17 个百分点，且增益可迁移至多个模型和运行框架。摘要未给出足以复现的方法细节，也未证明改进机制本身得到提升。
